core_message: In 1964 a survey team found an empty, unmarked lifeboat on the most remote island on Earth, and nobody has ever proven where it came from.
title: Who Left This Boat on the Loneliest Island on Earth?
description:
Bouvet Island is a small volcanic island in the far South Atlantic, almost entirely covered by a glacier. The nearest land, the coast of Antarctica, is about 1,700 km away. On 2 April 1964 a survey team led by Lieutenant Commander Allan Crawford was flown ashore by helicopter from HMS Protector. In a small lagoon on a lava shelf that had formed only a few years earlier, they found a half-swamped, unmarked whaler or ship's lifeboat. Nearby lay a pair of oars, a 44-gallon drum and a flattened copper tank. They found no camp and no remains, and they had about 45 minutes before they had to leave.

A biological survey visited the lagoon in 1966 and made no mention of the boat. Its origin has never been established.

3D scenes made in Blender with CC0 scanned textures and rocks from Poly Haven.

scenes.narration: In 1964, a helicopter dropped a survey team onto the loneliest island on Earth. In a small lagoon, they found a boat. There was nobody in it.
scenes.purpose: hook: an empty boat where no boat should be

scenes.narration: This is Bouvet Island, in the far South Atlantic. It is almost entirely covered by a glacier, and the nearest land, Antarctica, is about seventeen hundred kilometres away. Nobody lives here, and almost nobody ever visits.

The boat was a ship's lifeboat, half full of water, with no name and no markings. On the shore lay a pair of oars, an oil drum and a flattened copper tank. There was no camp, no message and no bodies.
Stranger still, the lagoon sat on a lava shelf that had only formed a few years earlier. So someone had landed here recently, on the most remote island in the world, and left without their boat.
scenes.purpose: why it cannot be an old wreck

scenes.narration: The team had less than an hour, so they flew away. When scientists came back two years later, there was no sign of the boat. Nobody has ever proven who it belonged to.
scenes.purpose: the boat vanishes, the mystery stays open
